 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. PHOENIX — The Arizona Diamondbacks have their priorities set for the offseason: get starting pitching, obtain a left-handed power bat, settle the first base position and acquire bullpen depth.
 However, ESPN ranks the Diamondbacks as the eighth-most likely team to land two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal, suggesting Arizona has at least a small chance of pursuing the left-hander.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Skubal finished his 2026 season with the Los Angeles Dodgers after spending six seasons with the Detroit Tigers. Now a free agent, the left-hander is drawing interest from several teams hoping to make a splash this offseason. But his projected price tag could limit realistic suitors.
 ESPN projects Skubal to receive a long-term contract worth over $300 million, but still ranks Arizona as the eighth-most likely team to land him this offseason.
 Jul 26, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) reacts after he gets a strike out to end the sixth inning against the Toronto Blue Jays at Comerica Park. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The D-Backs have gone down the big-contract route before, most notably with Zack Greinke's six-year, $206 million deal in 2016 and Corbin Burnes' six-year, $210 million contract signed before the 2025 season. Both investments have come with their challenges. Burnes suffered an elbow injury 11 starts into his Arizona tenure, requiring Tommy John surgery in June 2025. He returned to make just three starts in 2026, with four years remaining on his contract.
 That's what makes the D-Backs' potential pursuit of Skubal more of a long shot. After committing significant money to their pitching staff without getting the return they expected, the organization has reason to be cautious about another massive investment. Owner Ken Kendrick has also expressed interest in reducing payroll, making a contract of Skubal's projected size even more difficult to justify.
 Apr 1, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal in the first inning against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Arizona could also look to move on from other large contracts, including second baseman Ketel Marte, who has been involved in trade discussions with other teams. With the organization potentially looking to create more payroll flexibility, pursuing Skubal seems more unlikely than likely.
 Instead, ESPN believes the Diamondbacks should prioritize more affordable options, including right-hander Michael Soroka, who is coming off an efficient 2026 season. Soroka posted a 3.41 ERA and a 1.086 WHIP, with ESPN projecting him to receive a two-year, $24 million contract.
 ESPN also likes left-hander Foster Griffin, who is projected to receive a two-year, $30 million deal. Both pitchers would provide Arizona with starting rotation help without requiring the type of financial commitment Skubal would demand.
 May 17, 2024; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Detroit Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal (29) throws against the Arizona Diamondbacks in the first inning at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Rick Scuteri-USA TODAY Sports
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ultimately, the Snakes have to decide whether adding one of the best pitchers in baseball is worth the financial risk or if spreading that money across multiple needs would better serve the team.
 With starting pitching, a left-handed power bat and bullpen depth all on the offseason priority list, committing more than $350 million to one player could make addressing the rest of the roster even more difficult.
